body.statement:
For every \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every \(s_N\in(0,1]\) for which \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) is nonempty,
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}
\le \min\!\left\{1,4b_\lambda^2,\frac{C_0}{Ns_N^2}\right\},
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable estimators based on the entire observed sample. The covariance--PCA and APM least-squares estimator in \(\operatorname{def:pca\text{-}estimator}\) attains this upper bound, with \(C_0\) depending only on the fixed primitive radii and \((T,C)\).
body.justification: Evaluating the minimax infimum at the total covariance--PCA estimator gives the unconditional radius-adaptive upper bound; no positive universal lower bound is asserted.
body.gap: The result adds a fixed-panel complete-law upper guarantee with the primitive radius ceiling, while the same-shell target-separating construction required for a matching lower bound remains unavailable.
body.consumer: Users of \(\operatorname{apm}\) and \(\operatorname{fect}\) receive a sufficient finite-sample recovery guarantee rather than an overstated impossibility frontier.
